selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a dual-cavity bandpass filter topology optimized from recalled thin-film design principles. The hypothesis is that two Fabry-Perot cavities separated by distributed Bragg reflectors can simultaneously transmit the methane (3.25-3.35 μm) and CO2 (4.20-4.30 μm) bands while blocking the suppression bands. The design uses ZnS/MgF2 as the high/low index pair based on recalled IR transparency and index contrast. This route optimizes individual layer thicknesses while keeping the 22-layer topology fixed. What I would have wanted to look up: exact refractive indices of ZnS and MgF2 at 3-5 μm, CaF2 substrate index dispersion, and published dual-band filter designs for validation.

routes.title: Dual-cavity bandpass filter with ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer dual-cavity structure with ZnS/MgF2 quarter-wave-based stacks can achieve simultaneous transmission peaks at 3.30 μm and 4.25 μm with suppression in the 2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm bands when layer thicknesses are optimized.
routes.design_principle: Fabry-Perot cavities formed by low-index spacer layers between high-reflectivity DBR mirrors create transmission bands at wavelengths determined by cavity optical thickness. Two cavities with different thicknesses produce two passbands. Index contrast between ZnS (~2.3) and MgF2 (~1.35) provides sufficient reflectivity for blocking bands with limited layer count.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | Daimon-20
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 layers (within 24-layer limit)
All layers are dielectric (ZnS and MgF2 are conventionally depositable)
Layer thicknesses should remain within practical deposition ranges (50-2000 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: ZnS has high refractive index (~2.2-2.4) and good transmission in 3-5 μm IR range
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has low refractive index (~1.35-1.40) and is transparent in IR
Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with number of pairs and index contrast
Recalled knowledge: Fabry-Perot cavity transmission peak wavelength scales with cavity optical thickness (n×d)
Recalled knowledge: Dual-band filters can be constructed by cascading two cavities with different optical thicknesses
Recalled knowledge: Daimon-20 is a CaF2 dataset with index ~1.42-1.43 in this wavelength range
expected_advantages: ZnS/MgF2 pair provides high index contrast for efficient blocking with fewer layers
22-layer design leaves margin within the 24-layer constraint for potential refinement
Dual-cavity topology is a standard approach for multi-band transmission filters
All materials are from the guaranteed_names list and should resolve without ambiguity
known_risks: Uncertain about exact refractive indices of ZnS and MgF2 at 3-5 μm wavelengths - actual values may differ from recalled ~2.3 and ~1.35
Uncertain about Daimon-20 substrate index dispersion in this range - recalled value may not match dataset
Uncertain whether 22 layers is sufficient to achieve required blocking levels in suppression bands - may need more pairs
Recalled that ZnS may have some absorption features near 4-5 μm that could affect CO2 band transmission - would need to verify against actual dataset
The topology assumes normal incidence; if actual system uses oblique incidence, performance will shift
No polarization specification in request - design assumes unpolarized or normal incidence where polarization effects are minimal
Quarter-wave center wavelength selection is uncertain - chose 3.3 μm as compromise but 4.25 μm cavity may need different reference
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on Daimon-20 substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence from air side: ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, then Daimon-20 substrate. Optimize all 22 layer thicknesses individually to maximize transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands while minimizing transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. No metal layers. Total layer count is exactly 22. Materials are zns and mgf2 from the material catalog. Substrate is Daimon-20. Incidence is from air side at normal incidence (0 degrees). Wavelength range of interest is 2500-5000 nm.
